data.description: Atin decision 2026-10-01. Keep two channels: c11 send stays the plain explicit poke; the mailbox becomes the durable channel. Record both with full text, and have c11 write a live self-contained HTML page of all agent traffic. Today agents use only c11 send because mailbox push gates on shell promptIdle and never reaches a running agent (166 buffered, 2 flushed all-time), and c11 send leaves no trace in any log. Built as five parallel lanes against pinned contracts (see plan): A record every send as a tab.input_sent event and put bodies on mailbox events; B push mail when the agent is waiting, not when the shell is idle; C drain inboxes at turn boundaries through Claude, Codex and Grok hooks; D c11 writes messages.html and c11 messages view opens it; E mailbox --help fix and skill teaching. Design reference for D: the Overwatch prototype at code/overwatch/tools/mailbox-viz/. Done when one tagged build passes Atin's numbered sign-off script.
data.title: Agent messaging: record every send, deliver mail to waiting agents, and a live messages page

data.body:
Finding from the Overwatch prototype (code/overwatch/tools/mailbox-viz, built from all 37 workspaces' dispatch logs): 52 real inbox copies failed with `_copy eio` and were lost for good. Every one went to a recipient whose tab title contains `/` or is 78-105 bytes long; no title over 27 bytes ever got an inbox copy. All 20 scan-cartographer messages died because the recipient's title was a path (`.../Stage11/scanner-worktrees/scan-15-space`); 28 Adoption-run messages to long `MRQ-2xx [status]: ...` titles died the same way. Correlation, not confirmed cause, but the inbox directory is keyed on the raw title.

Folded into Lane B (it owns delivery): key inbox directories on something filesystem-safe and stable (the tab UUID, or a sanitized `mailbox.address`), never the raw title; keep title-based addressing as a lookup only. Accept: a send to a tab titled `a/b: c` with a 100-byte title lands in its inbox and drains. Also: the Adoption Orchestrator still has 90 unread envelopes from the Aug 15 run, so `recv --drain` was never called at turn boundaries there; Lane C fixes that.

Orchestrator: contract clarifications pinned before dispatch (binding for all lanes; change only by comment here, Orchestrator broadcasts).

C1-wire. C1's JSON is the logical shape. Fit it to the real envelope in Sources/Events/EventEnvelope.swift: the target tab goes in the envelope's existing tab/surface field (follow the wire convention main uses today), the `data` fields go in the payload exactly as named in C1. Lane A posts the exact emitted JSON line for one `send` and one `send-key` as an "A:" comment as soon as it exists; Lane D builds fixtures from that line.

C2-impl. Exact signature, owned by Lane A. Lanes B and C copy it byte-for-byte only if their branch needs it, so the merge is clean:

    func emitMailboxDelivered(
        workspace: UUID,
        id: String,
        recipient: String,
        surface: UUID?,
        via: String = "inbox"
    ) {
        emit(
            .mailboxDelivered,
            workspace: workspace,
            surface: surface,
            payload: ["id": id, "recipient": recipient, "via": via]
        )
    }

`via` values: "push" (Lane B stdin push), "drain" (Lane C recv --drain / hook drain), "inbox" (file landed in the inbox). A drain from the CLI process reaches the app through the socket; Lane C owns that path.

C3-order. Claim before inject. A consumer renames `<inbox>/<ULID>.msg` to `<inbox>/_read/<ULID>.msg` before it types or prints the message; if injection fails, it renames the file back. Reason: Lane B's injected turn fires Lane C's UserPromptSubmit hook, which must not find the same envelope still in the inbox root.

C5 (new). Inbox directory key = the recipient tab's UUID (lowercased), not its title. Title and mailbox.address stay as lookups that resolve to tab UUIDs. `recv` also reads the legacy title-keyed directory when it exists, so old unread mail is not stranded. Lane B owns `MailboxLayout.inboxURL` and `resolveMailboxCaller` (app and CLI); no other lane edits them. Lane C's drain keeps calling them and changes only what happens to each entry (claim per C3, hook-format output).

C6 (new). Lane C runs under the CLAUDE.md principle "c11 never writes tenant config; PATH wrappers under Resources/bin are the only rail." Claude hooks go through `Resources/bin/claude --settings` (already allowed). For Codex and Grok, Lane C first looks for a per-launch, no-persistent-write path through their wrappers. If none exists, it sends a DECISION to the Orchestrator rather than writing into ~/.codex or ~/.grok.

A: plan
Implement the C1 event contract at the existing event envelope/emitter seam, with a pure payload builder that resolves caller attribution, captures text/key sends, computes byte counts, and truncates only above 256 KiB on a UTF-8 boundary. Wire every socket send variant after a successful PTY write, preserving the existing target tab/surface envelope field and avoiding typing paths. Extend mailbox accepted/delivered emitters and the inbox landing call site with the pinned C2 fields/signature, then update the events reference taxonomy. Add behavioral c11-logic coverage for text/key/null caller/truncation and run a tagged build proof for send, send-key, and outside-c11 attribution. Cut line: only Lane A owned Sources/Events, socket send seams, mailbox event/inbox landing code, the events reference, and focused tests; no skill sync, no other lanes, no merge.

E: plan
Fix the CLI help pre-check for mailbox and audit sibling families for the same mismatch; preserve existing command behavior and note the messages/mailbox-view addition Lane D must make. Draft the skill card, orchestration reference, and mailbox guide overview/teaching against the two-channel contract, leaving delivery/drain mechanics to B/C. Validate with focused help tests if available, then a tagged CLI proof of --help, -h, and one real subcommand; commit and push phase 1 plus drafts, without syncing installed skills or opening the PR until the Orchestrator signals final behavior.

C: harness hook paths (C6 findings, verified against the installed CLIs: codex-cli 0.159.3, grok 1.0.46)

**Codex: per-launch path exists, no persistent write. Building it.**
- Codex reads inline hooks from any config layer, including the `-c` session-flags layer: `-c 'hooks.Stop=[{hooks=[{type="command",command="…",timeout=10}]}]'` is accepted.
- Non-managed hooks are skipped until trusted. Trust is `hooks.state."<key>".trusted_hash`, and `hook_states_from_stack` (codex-rs/hooks/src/config_rules.rs) reads state from the **User and SessionFlags layers only**, so trust can also ride in on `-c`.
- Key for a `-c` hook: `/<session-flags>/config.toml:<event_label>:<group>:<handler>` (e.g. `…:stop:0:0`). The dotted key form `-c 'hooks.state."/<session-flags>/config.toml:…".trusted_hash=…'` is mis-split ("ignored" warning); the inline-table form works: `-c 'hooks.state={"/<session-flags>/config.toml:user_prompt_submit:0:0"={trusted_hash="sha256:…"}}'`.
- Hash = `sha256` of compact, key-sorted JSON `{"event_name":"<label>","hooks":[{"async":false,"command":"…","timeout":N,"type":"command"}]}` (codex-rs/config/src/fingerprint.rs `version_for_toml`). Reproduced byte-exact against an existing trusted hook in ~/.codex/config.toml; the wrapper computes it with `shasum` at launch.
- Proof (`codex exec`, scratch dir): the trusted `-c` UserPromptSubmit hook fired and received `{"session_id","turn_id","transcript_path","cwd","hook_event_name":"UserPromptSubmit","model","permission_mode","prompt"}`; the user's own ~/.codex/hooks.json SessionStart hook still fired alongside it (layers merge; the session-flags `hooks.state` table does not shadow user trust). Nothing written under ~/.codex.
- Stop: `{"decision":"block","reason":…}` makes Codex continue with a continuation prompt; input carries `stop_hook_active`.

**Grok: no per-launch path for the interactive TUI. DECISION sent to the Orchestrator.**
- Hook sources (docs `~/.grok/docs/user-guide/10-hooks.md`): `~/.grok/hooks/*.json`, `~/.grok/config.toml`, `~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.cursor/hooks.json`, project `.grok/`/`.claude/`/`.cursor/` (need folder trust), managed/requirements TOML, and plugins.
- `GROK_CONFIG` / `GROK_CONFIG_PATH` overlays are allowlisted (models, features, toolset, shell env filter) and documented as unable to "spawn commands … or add a discovery source"; hooks are dropped.
- `--plugin-dir` (auto-trusted, per process) exists only on `grok agent … stdio` and is ignored in leader mode; the TUI rejects it (`unexpected argument '--plugin-dir'`).
- A temp `GROK_HOME` overlay would relocate sessions/auth/leader socket (and break the wrapper's session-resume capture); rejected as unsafe.
- Grok semantics worth knowing either way: UserPromptSubmit `additionalContext` is **discarded** by Grok ("an allowing hook's stdout / additionalContext is discarded"), so Grok can drain only at Stop (`decision:block` + reason, input `stopHookActive`, `reason=="end_turn"` filter for the session-end Stop fire, hard cap 8 continuations/turn).

C: plan

**Architecture**
- New `Sources/Mailbox/MailboxDrain.swift` (pure logic, app + CLI targets): `claim(entry)` renames `<inbox>/<ULID>.msg` → `<inbox>/_read/<ULID>.msg` (rename is the lock; ENOENT = another consumer won, skip), `unclaim` renames back; `drain(inboxURL:)` returns claimed envelopes in ULID order; `hookOutput(format:event:framed:)` renders per-harness JSON. Framing via a new shared `MailboxFraming.framedBlock` (same bytes as `StdinMailboxHandler.formatFramedBlock`; a logic test pins equality so the two cannot drift; Lane B's file is untouched).
- `c11 mailbox recv`: per-entry loop changes only. Plain `--drain` claims to `_read/` instead of unlinking. New `--hook-format claude|codex|grok` (event from the hook's stdin `hook_event_name`, override with `--event prompt-submit|stop`). Output: prompt-submit → `{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":…}}`; stop → `{"decision":"block","reason":…}`. Empty inbox / any error → no output, exit 0. `MailboxLayout.inboxURL` and `resolveMailboxCaller` untouched (C5).
- Stop loop safety: never claim when `stop_hook_active` / `stopHookActive` is true (mail waits for the next boundary or Lane B's push), Grok also requires `reason=="end_turn"`; block only when ≥1 envelope was actually claimed. So a delivered turn always ends at the next Stop.
- Grok prompt-submit: no claim (Grok discards that context), mail waits for Stop or push.
- `mailbox.delivered` `via:"drain"`: new v2 socket method `mailbox.report_delivered` (off-main, no `main.sync`), one per claimed envelope, best-effort (socket down never fails the hook). `EventEmitter.emitMailboxDelivered` copied byte-for-byte from C2-impl.
- Claude: fold into the existing `c11 claude-hook prompt-submit|stop` (one hook process per event, no `HOOKS_JSON` change). Stop drains first; when it delivers it reports `working` and skips the idle status/notification. Prompt-submit stops printing the bare `OK` (Claude injects UserPromptSubmit stdout as context) and prints the JSON only when mail exists.
- Codex: `Resources/bin/codex` adds `-c hooks.UserPromptSubmit/Stop=…` + `-c hooks.state={…trusted_hash…}` per launch (see `C: harness hook paths`), command = absolute bundle `c11 mailbox recv --drain --hook-format codex`.
- Grok: pending DECISION; the CLI `--hook-format grok` ships regardless.
- Docs: drain/hook section of `docs/c11-mailbox-guide.md`.

**Tests (c11-logic, new `MailboxDrainTests`)**: claim moves to `_read/`; second claimer skips; unclaim restores; ULID order; hook JSON for each harness × event; stop_hook_active / stopHookActive / grok non-end_turn → nothing; empty → nothing; framing equality with StdinMailboxHandler.

**Runtime proof (tagged `c11-257-c`)**: Claude mid-turn mail lands once at the next boundary; Codex same; racing `recv --drain` vs hook drain delivers each envelope once and `_read/` holds it; empty hook <100 ms; Stop-delivered turn stops normally after.

**Cut line**: Grok wiring waits on the DECISION; everything else ships in this PR.

B: plan

**Waiting signal per harness (established by reading the code).** c11's `waiting.entered` is a workspace-level unread-notification edge, and the derived `activity` key also flips to idle on every agent notification, including Claude's permission prompts. Neither is safe to paste into. Lane B gates on a narrower per-tab truth, the agent turn edge:
- at prompt: an explicit `report_agent_activity idle` (Claude Stop hook and SessionStart, Codex wrapper launch seed) or a Codex turn-complete notify (`legacy_codex_notify_payload_b64` on `notification.create_for_tab`, already thread-filtered).
- working: `report_agent_activity working` (Claude prompt-submit) or any submit Return into the tab (operator, text box, `c11 send`, our own push).
- Grok has no lifecycle signal today (its tab sticks at working after the first Return). Best available: Grok writes `turn_started`/`turn_ended` to `~/.grok/sessions/<cwd>/<id>/events.jsonl`. The Grok wrapper's existing background session watcher tails that file and reports `agent-hook working|idle`, plus an idle seed at launch. Per-launch, no persistent writes (C6). Limit: `grok --continue` gives no session id, so no turn signal for that launch.
- Notification-sourced idle never opens the gate. Claude SessionStart with `source:"compact"` no longer reports idle (it fires mid-turn).

**Gate** (`MailboxStdinBuffer`, pure, clock-injected):
- Shell at `promptIdle`: today's rule (inject); an agent that exited to the shell drops its buffered agent entries (the inbox still holds them).
- Agent tab (turn record present, or detected agent kind): inject only when at prompt, and the at-prompt edge is newer than our last push (stops a double push in the 200 ms before the Return lands). Working or no record: buffer.
- Operator draft: any operator keystroke into the PTY after the at-prompt edge defers the push until the next turn boundary. No timeout: pasting after a quiet window would still splice onto a draft and submit it. A new `lastOperatorKeyAt` is stamped from the same `Date` as the existing touched clock (no new allocation on keyDown). Clicks and text-box typing do not count (the text box is not the PTY composer). Ghost suggestions are not input.
- Flush runs on every at-prompt edge. All buffered agent entries go in one paste and one submit (one turn).
- Freshness: agent entries never expire (64-entry cap still evicts oldest). Shell entries keep the 10-minute window.

**C3 consume.** At inject time (immediate or flush) rename `<inbox>/<ULID>.msg` → `<inbox>/_read/<ULID>.msg` first; ENOENT → skip silently (new dispatch-log outcome `skipped`); if the tab is gone at inject → rename back. Emit `mailbox.delivered` `via:"push"` (C2-impl signature copied byte-for-byte). Typing goes through `sendSubmitFormText` (the `c11 send` paste + delayed Return path, safe for background tabs).

**C5 inbox keying. New shapes, so Lane C can build against them now:**
- `MailboxLayout.inboxURL(state:workspaceId:tabId: UUID) -> URL` (non-throwing) → `<mailboxes>/<tab-uuid-lowercased>/`
- `MailboxLayout.legacyInboxURL(state:workspaceId:tabName:) -> URL?` (nil when the title is not path-safe)
- `MailboxLayout.recvInboxURLs(state:workspaceId:tabId:tabName:) -> [URL]` (canonical, then legacy when it exists)
- `MailboxLayout.readURL(inbox:)` → `<inbox>/_read/`; `MailboxIO.claim(id:inbox:) throws -> URL?` and `MailboxIO.unclaim(id:inbox:)`. Lane C can reuse these.
- CLI `resolveMailboxCaller(client:fromOverride:surfaceOverride:)` keeps its name and labels and returns `(workspaceId: UUID, tabName: String, tabId: UUID?)`. `--surface <name>` resolves to a tab UUID through `mailbox.resolve` scoped to the caller's workspace. `recv` iterates `recvInboxURLs`; `inbox-dir` prints the canonical path.
- EIO cause: confirmed by reading. `copyToInbox` calls `inboxURL(tabName: title)`, whose `validateSurfaceName` throws on `/` or more than 64 bytes; the catch logs `_copy eio`. A runtime before/after proof goes in validation.

**Files:** `Sources/Mailbox/{MailboxStdinBuffer,StdinMailboxHandler,MailboxLayout,MailboxIO,MailboxDispatcher,MailboxDispatchLog}.swift`, `Sources/Workspace.swift` (writer/flush), `Sources/TabLivenessDeriver.swift` (source-tagged lifecycle), report_agent_activity handlers, `NotificationHandlers.swift` (Codex edge), `GhosttyTerminalView.swift` (key clock), `Events/EventEmitter.swift` (C2-impl), `CLI/c11.swift` (caller/recv/inbox-dir, SessionStart compact guard), `Resources/bin/grok` (turn tail), `docs/c11-mailbox-guide.md` delivery section. Possible overlap with Lane C: `Resources/bin/grok` and the `recv` loop. My edits are separate blocks.

**Tests (c11-logic):** gate decisions (shell, agent at prompt, working, unknown, stale edge vs last push, draft pending), agent entries not expiring, one-paste flush join; claim/unclaim/ENOENT skip; inbox key (UUID lowercased, `a/b: c` 100-byte title, legacy dir read); dispatcher copies into the UUID dir for a slash/long title.

**Runtime proof:** tagged `c11-257-b`, accept 1–5 for Claude, Codex `--yolo` and Grok `--always-approve`; trace lines and screenshots.

**Cut line:** if the Grok tail proves unreliable live, Grok falls back to buffer plus Lane C drain, and I report that.

Orchestrator: C6 Grok ruling (Atin 2026-10-01: leans plugin, flexible). Default: no write to ~/.grok; Grok mail lands via Lane B's push at the waiting edge, driven by the grok wrapper tailing the session events.jsonl. Fallback, pre-approved: if Lane B's live Grok proof shows that signal unreliable, Lane C adds an opt-in Agent Skills install of a c11-owned Grok plugin (~/.grok/plugins/c11-mailbox/, one Stop hook, idempotent, removable, no-op outside c11), following the existing OpenCode plugin precedent in SkillInstaller. Codex: per-launch -c hooks, no ~/.codex write.

A: validation
- Baseline and post-change focused logic run: scripts/with-build-lock.sh xcodebuild -project GhosttyTabs.xcodeproj -scheme c11-logic -configuration Debug -destination "platform=macOS" test -only-testing:c11LogicTests/EventLogTests; ** TEST SUCCEEDED **, 17 tests, 0 failures.
- Static gate: git diff --check passed.
- Tagged build/app: ./scripts/reload.sh --tag c11-257-a; ** BUILD SUCCEEDED **. QA launch: ./scripts/launch-tagged-automation.sh c11-257-a --qa fresh. Tagged process and /tmp/c11-debug-c11-257-a.sock were live.
- C1 runtime on workspace 63916DB4-C544-4057-8755-F290FDCA0B12: tagged CLI send reached target tab 92D986CC-57AA-48D2-8FB1-E991E569C144 with caller 32B556C8-A907-4B4E-BC22-5A7ED82DA08C; send-key enter reached the same PTY; a send with all caller env aliases unset emitted null caller attribution. Exact C1 wire samples are in the earlier A: C1-wire sample comment.
- C2 runtime: the tagged c11 binary's pre-dispatch allowlist still rejects `c11 mailbox send` (Lane E owns that CLI seam), so I wrote one valid v1 envelope atomically to the tagged workspace _outbox and exercised MailboxDispatcher/inbox landing. It emitted:

B: validation

Tagged build `c11-257-b` (launched with `launch-tagged-automation.sh c11-257-b --qa fresh`, socket `/tmp/c11-debug-c11-257-b.sock`). Recipients were launched inside the tagged build with `launch-agent`: Claude (`--model sonnet`, bypass permissions), Codex (`--yolo`, cwd `/private/tmp`, an already-trusted folder, so no trust write to `~/.codex`), and Grok (`--always-approve`). Each was told "reply with one word". `mailbox.delivery=stdin` was set on all three. Mail came from a `sender` tab via the tagged CLI (`c11 mailbox send`).

**EIO before.** Production dispatch logs hold 52 `_copy eio` entries, every one to a title with `/` or 78-105 bytes (e.g. 81-byte `MRQ-234 [review]: ...`). The longest title that ever got an inbox copy is 27 bytes. Cause confirmed in code: `copyToInbox` → `inboxURL(tabName:)` → `validateSurfaceName` throws on `/` or more than 64 bytes → caught as `_copy eio`.

1. **Waiting agent, new turn within ~1 s:** PASS for all three. Sent 17:32:10-11. Read-screen 1.5 s later: Claude had already answered `PONG`, Codex was "Working (2s)" on the `<c11-msg>` turn, and Grok was "Waiting for response 1.8s". Trace for each: `received → resolved → copied → handler stdin ok → cleaned`. Envelopes were claimed into `<inbox>/_read/` (inbox root empty).
2. **Mid-turn agent, lands at turn end:** PASS for all three.
   - Codex (`sleep 25` turn): `buffered` 00:32:39.855Z → `flushed` 00:33:07.477Z. The message arrived as its own turn after the sleep turn, and Codex replied `PONG2`.
   - Grok: `buffered` 00:32:40.247Z → `flushed` 00:33:07.413Z, `PONG2`. This turn edge comes from the new wrapper watcher on `events.jsonl` (`turn_ended` → `agent-hook idle`).
   - Claude (foreground `sleep 20` turn): `buffered` 00:33:38.913Z → `flushed` 00:33:55.555Z. The screen shows `SLEPT`, then the `<c11-msg>` turn, then `PONG3`.
   - On the first busy attempt Claude put the sleep in the background and ended its turn, so the mail was pushed at once. That is correct, because the agent was at its prompt.
3. **Codex and Grok:** covered in 1 and 2 above.
4. **`a/b: c` + 100-byte title:** PASS. Trace: `received → resolved → copied → cleaned`, with no `_copy`. The file landed in `mailboxes/de4f5f1c-…/` (lowercased tab UUID). `recv --drain` as that tab printed the envelope and emptied the inbox. `inbox-dir` prints the UUID path. Legacy read: an envelope placed in a title-keyed `mailboxes/legacy-rcpt/` directory and a new one in the UUID inbox both printed from one `recv --drain` in ULID order, and both directories were left empty.
5. **Operator draft:** unit-covered only (`testOperatorDraftDefersUntilSubmit`, `testSubmitKeystrokeIsNotADraft`). The guard reads a new `lastOperatorKeyAt`, which only a real keyDown stamps. Socket `send` and `debug.type` do not stamp it (`debug.type` also activates the app and steals the operator's focus), so a live proof needs a human keyboard. **Sign-off step for Atin:** in a waiting Claude tab with `mailbox.delivery=stdin`, type `hello wor` without Enter. Send mail to it. The draft is untouched and `trace` shows `buffered`. Finish the line and press Enter. After that turn ends, the mail lands as its own turn (`flushed`).
6. **c11-logic unit tests:** `MailboxStdinBufferTests`, `MailboxLayoutTests`, `MailboxIOTests`, `MailboxDispatcherTests`: 61 tests, 0 failures, `** TEST SUCCEEDED **` (re-run after the rebase onto `0ff8887e5e`).

**C3 race, live:** I made Codex busy, sent mail, and ran `recv --drain` as the Codex tab before its turn ended. Trace: `buffered` → `skipped`, and Codex was typed nothing. `mailbox.delivered` events for the run: 7 × `via:"push"` (3 waiting + 3 busy + Claude busy retry) plus `via:"inbox"` copies.

**Rebased head smoke** (`bd0b139b3e` on `0ff8887e5e`, fresh tagged build): waiting Claude `ok` + `PONG`; busy Grok `buffered` 00:38:51.887Z → `flushed` 00:39:05.082Z, `PONG2` after `SLEPT`.

Evidence files (Lane B scratchpad): `evidence/dispatch.log`, `evidence/delivered-events.ndjson`, `evidence/screen-tab{6,9,8}.txt`.

Integration notes for the Orchestrator:
(a) Lane C's Claude Stop-hook drain and my Stop-hook push can race. C3 makes that safe: whichever renames first wins, and the other logs `skipped`.
(b) `Resources/bin/grok` gained a self-contained `grok_watch_turns` block plus an idle seed. If Lane C edits the same wrapper, both blocks merge side by side.
(c) Grok launched with `--continue` reports no turn edges. Its mail buffers and the inbox floor holds it.

D: plan

Architecture: add a pure messages-page data model and renderer plus an app-owned writer under the existing event/state seams. The writer will observe C1/C2 events, debounce off-main, rebuild on startup from the event log plus mailbox inbox history, cap embedded records with the bound stated in the page, escape all agent text, use safe JSON script embedding and a restrictive no-network CSP, and atomically replace an owner-only messages.html.

CLI/browser: add messages view with mailbox view as a hidden alias, reuse an existing messages browser tab, and reload that tab on file changes without a localhost server. Add runtime tests for fixture shaping, both channels and lifecycle joins, escaping/script-breakout resistance, the data bound, and writer persistence/atomic output. Add the mailbox guide and CLI API docs. Use fixture C1/C2 wire data until Lane A is integrated; do not modify the Overwatch prototype. Cut line: tagged live proof follows Lane A/C/E integration.

C: validation (head 9841c40621, tagged build `c11-257-c`, launched with `launch-tagged-automation.sh c11-257-c --qa fresh`; Lane B absent on this branch, recipients had no `mailbox.delivery`, so the hook drain was the only consumer)

**Accept 1, Claude mid-turn, exactly once.** Claude (sonnet) told to `sleep 30` then reply TASK-DONE; `c11 mailbox send --to lc-claude --body VIOLET-MOTH-3` sent mid-turn at 00:43:32Z. The envelope stayed in the inbox until the turn boundary, then the Stop hook (`c11 claude-hook stop`) claimed it and blocked the stop; Claude's next turn printed `MAIL-SEEN: VIOLET-MOTH-3` and stopped (idle prompt). Events: `mailbox.delivered via:"inbox"` seq 28, then exactly one `via:"drain"` seq 33 at 00:43:53Z. First run (earlier build, same path): ORANGE-KITE-42 via Stop; then BLUE-HERON-7 sent while idle + a new prompt reached Claude through UserPromptSubmit `additionalContext`; asked to list every mailbox body it had received, Claude answered `BODY: ORANGE-KITE-42 / BODY: BLUE-HERON-7 / COUNT:2`.
**Accept 2, Codex mid-turn, exactly once.** Same task in `codex --yolo` through the tagged `Resources/bin/codex` (per-launch `-c` hooks + trust). Mail AMBER-WREN-8 mid-turn.
